name: 3DCP Velocity
desc: Compute the nozzle velocity for 3D concrete printing based on the material flow velocity, nozzle diameter, layer width and nozzle height. The analytical expressions were derived from (Alhussain et al., 2024) and tunned based on experimental data and regression analysis collected at the ARENA Lab of the School of Architecture Art and Design of the University of Minho.

inputs.name: Material Extrusion Velocity
inputs.desc: The material extrusion velocity in millimeters per second (mm/s)

inputs.name: Nozzle Diameter
inputs.desc: The nozzle diameter in millimeters (mm)

inputs.name: Filament Width
inputs.desc: The filament width in millimeters (mm)

inputs.name: Nozzle Height
inputs.desc: The nozzle height in millimeters (mm). Nozzle height can be considered equal to filament height if the extrusion is kept with adequate bounds, roughly between 1.7 and 2.3 width ratios.

outputs.name: Nozzle Velocity
outputs.desc: The nozzle velocity in meters per second (m/s)

outputs.name: Contact Width
outputs.desc: The contact width in millimeters (mm)

outputs.name: Height Ratio
outputs.desc: The ratio between the Nozzle Heigth and the Nozzle Diameter

outputs.name: Width Ratio
outputs.desc: The ratio between the Filament Width and Nozzle Diameter

name: Bridge Cell Tree
desc: Joins planar cells with width corridors between their centroids using an indexed tree of cell neighbors.

inputs.name: Cells
inputs.desc: Closed coplanar cell boundaries. Cell indices follow the input list order.

inputs.name: Neighbors
inputs.desc: Neighbor indices for each cell. Branch {i} contains the indices connected to cell i.

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Total width of each centroid connection corridor.

inputs.name: Inset Cells
inputs.desc: Inset every cell by half the corridor width before joining.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Optional common working plane. When omitted, the plane is inferred from the first cell.

outputs.name: Boundaries
outputs.desc: Closed boundaries produced by uniting the cells and centroid corridors.

outputs.name: Connections
outputs.desc: Centroid-to-centroid connections represented by the validated tree.

name: Bridge Cells
desc: Joins planar cell boundaries with a corridor around an open polyline path to create a continuous closed toolpath.

inputs.name: Cells
inputs.desc: Closed coplanar cell boundaries to join.

inputs.name: Path
inputs.desc: Open polyline path crossing the cells in the order they are to be joined.

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Total width of the connecting corridor, or filament layer width.

inputs.name: Inset Cells
inputs.desc: Inset every cell by half the corridor width (or half of the filament layer width) before joining.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Optional common working plane. When omitted, the plane is inferred from the path.

outputs.name: Boundaries
outputs.desc: Closed boundaries produced by uniting the cells and connecting corridor.

name: Edge Aligned Bounding Rectangle
desc: Constructs the bounding rectangle of a planar polygon aligned to the direction of a selected input polyline edge. Bounding extents are computed from the polygon convex hull.

inputs.name: Polyline
inputs.desc: Closed planar polyline.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Reference plane of the polygon.

inputs.name: Edge Index
inputs.desc: Zero-based index of the input polyline edge whose direction is used to align the rectangle. The index refers to the cleaned input polyline order, not the convex hull edge order.

outputs.name: Rectangle
outputs.desc: Edge-aligned bounding rectangle.

outputs.name: Area
outputs.desc: Rectangle area.

outputs.name: Length
outputs.desc: Rectangle length along the selected edge direction.

outputs.name: Width
outputs.desc: Rectangle width perpendicular to the selected edge direction.

outputs.name: Convex Hull
outputs.desc: Convex hull used to compute the rectangle extents.

name: Eulerian Path
desc: Finds an Eulerian path through a connected network of curves.

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Connected curve network. Each curve is treated as one graph edge.

inputs.name: Start
inputs.desc: Start point. The closest graph endpoint is used.

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Endpoint merge tolerance.

outputs.name: Path
outputs.desc: Eulerian path curves, oriented in traversal order.

outputs.name: Exists
outputs.desc: True when an Eulerian path exists from the selected start vertex.

name: 3DCP Extrusion Profile
desc: Creates a closed extrusion mesh with a rounded-rectangle bead profile along a toolpath.

inputs.name: Toolpath
inputs.desc: Toolpath curve along which the extrusion profile is generated.

inputs.name: Layer Width
inputs.desc: Extruded layer width in model units.

inputs.name: Layer Height
inputs.desc: Extruded layer height in model units.

inputs.name: Sampling Distance
inputs.desc: Approximate distance between mesh profile rings.

inputs.name: Profile Tolerance
inputs.desc: Maximum chord deviation used to discretize the profile and end caps.

inputs.name: Fillet Radius
inputs.desc: Toolpath corner fillet radius. Use zero for half the layer width.

inputs.name: Printing Plane
inputs.desc: Plane whose normal defines the printing vertical direction.

outputs.name: Mesh
outputs.desc: Closed extrusion-profile mesh.

outputs.name: Filleted Curve
outputs.desc: Toolpath curve after corner filleting.

name: Five-Segment Arch
desc: Constructs a five-segment arch using Michal's radius-ratio method.

inputs.name: Span
inputs.desc: Overall width of the arch.

inputs.name: Rise
inputs.desc: Vertical height from the spring line to the apex.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Construction plane. Span follows its X axis and rise follows its Y axis.

outputs.name: Arch
outputs.desc: Five-segment polycurve arch.

outputs.name: Arc Segments
outputs.desc: The five individual arc segments from left to right.

outputs.name: Centers
outputs.desc: Centers of the five arc segments.

outputs.name: Joints
outputs.desc: Junction points between consecutive arc segments.

outputs.name: Michal Ratio
outputs.desc: First-radius factor calculated by Michal's linear fit.

outputs.name: Apex
outputs.desc: Apex point of the arch.

name: Hamiltonian Path
desc: Finds a Hamiltonian vertex path in a connected curve network. Uses exact dynamic programming for small graphs and beam search for larger graphs.

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Connected curve network. Curve endpoints define graph vertices.

inputs.name: Start
inputs.desc: Start point. The closest graph vertex is used.

inputs.name: Use Exact
inputs.desc: If true, use exact dynamic programming up to 23 vertices, then fall back to beam search. If false, use beam search directly.

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Endpoint snap tolerance.

outputs.name: Points
outputs.desc: Hamiltonian vertex order from start to end.

outputs.name: Path
outputs.desc: Polyline through the Hamiltonian vertex order.

outputs.name: Full
outputs.desc: True if the returned path visits every vertex in the start component.

name: Ice Ray Lattice
desc: Subdivides a convex planar polygon into smaller polygons using an iterative Ice Ray splitting strategy.

inputs.name: Polygon
inputs.desc: Closed convex planar polyline to subdivide.

inputs.name: Max Area
inputs.desc: Maximum target area for each polygon.

inputs.name: Cut Ratio
inputs.desc: Normalized cut range on each chosen side. Must satisfy 0 < R < 1.

inputs.name: Side Ratio
inputs.desc: Minimum side-length factor relative to average side length for a side to be eligible for splitting.

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.desc: Random seed.

outputs.name: Polygons
outputs.desc: Subdivided polygons.

name: L Component
desc: Creates the closed polyline of an L corner connection from a construction plane, two arm directions, per-arm widths and per-arm minimum member lengths measured beyond the joint geometry.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Construction plane. Its origin defines the corner origin.

inputs.name: Vector A
inputs.desc: First arm direction.

inputs.name: Vector B
inputs.desc: Second arm direction.

inputs.name: Widths
inputs.desc: Per-arm widths. If fewer values are provided than arms, the last value is repeated.

inputs.name: Min Member Lengths
inputs.desc: Per-arm minimum member lengths measured beyond the resolved joint. If fewer values are provided than arms, the last value is repeated.

outputs.name: Polyline
outputs.desc: Closed L-component polyline.

outputs.name: Vertices
outputs.desc: Polyline vertices in order.

name: Metric Subdivision
desc: Subdivides a length by maximizing the use of a preferred maximum module length while enforcing a minimum allowable remainder length.

inputs.name: Length
inputs.desc: Total length to subdivide.

inputs.name: Max Length
inputs.desc: Preferred maximum module length.

inputs.name: Min Length
inputs.desc: Minimum acceptable remainder or end-segment length.

outputs.name: Centers
outputs.desc: Segment center positions measured from zero.

outputs.name: Lengths
outputs.desc: Segment lengths.

outputs.name: Count
outputs.desc: Number of segments.

name: Minimum Bounding Rectangle
desc: Constructs a robust minimum-area bounding rectangle for a planar polygon by evaluating all convex-hull edge-aligned candidates.

inputs.name: Polyline
inputs.desc: Closed planar polyline.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Reference plane of the polygon.

outputs.name: Rectangle
outputs.desc: Minimum-area bounding rectangle.

outputs.name: Area
outputs.desc: Rectangle area.

outputs.name: Length
outputs.desc: Rectangle length along its local x-axis.

outputs.name: Width
outputs.desc: Rectangle width along its local y-axis.

outputs.name: Frame
outputs.desc: Rectangle local frame.

outputs.name: Convex Hull
outputs.desc: Convex hull used in the computation.

name: Miter Component
desc: Creates one closed polyline miter-joint component per wall direction from a construction plane, wall directions, arm lengths and widths.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Construction plane. Its origin defines the joint center.

inputs.name: Vectors
inputs.desc: Wall directions meeting at the joint.

inputs.name: Arm Lengths
inputs.desc: Per-arm lengths. If fewer values are provided than vectors, the last value is repeated.

inputs.name: Widths
inputs.desc: Per-arm widths. If fewer values are provided than vectors, the last value is repeated.

inputs.name: Min Angle
inputs.desc: Minimum angular separation in degrees for distinct wall directions.

outputs.name: Components
outputs.desc: One closed miter component polyline per wall direction.

outputs.name: Leg Points
outputs.desc: Center points at the end of each arm.

name: N Component
desc: Creates the closed polyline of a multi-wall intersection component from a construction plane, wall directions, per-arm widths and per-arm minimum member lengths measured beyond the joint geometry.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Construction plane. Its origin defines the component center.

inputs.name: Vectors
inputs.desc: Wall directions meeting at the intersection.

inputs.name: Min Member Lengths
inputs.desc: Per-arm minimum member lengths measured beyond the resolved joint. If fewer values are provided than directions, the last value is repeated.

inputs.name: Widths
inputs.desc: Per-arm widths. If fewer values are provided than directions, the last value is repeated.

inputs.name: Min Angle
inputs.desc: Minimum angular separation in degrees for distinct wall directions.

outputs.name: Polyline
outputs.desc: Closed N-component polyline.

outputs.name: Leg Points
outputs.desc: Stub center points for each wall direction.

name: Offset
desc: Offset description

inputs.name: Polyline
inputs.desc: A planar polyline

inputs.name: Weights
inputs.desc: A list of weights per edge, by default a constant weight of 1 is assumed for all sides. Weights can be understood as the cotangent of the roof angle.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: The plane on which the curve lies

inputs.name: Type
inputs.desc: True for Multiplicative weights (edge speed = w) and false for Additive weights (edge speed = 1 + wa)

inputs.name: Direction
inputs.desc: Offset only inside - 0; offset only outside - 1; offset both sides - 2

inputs.name: Distances
inputs.desc: offset-spec = <one-block> [ ',' <one-block> [ ',' ... ] ]   one - block = < one - offset > ['+' < one - offset > ['+'... ]]  one - offset = [< cnt > '*'] < time >  examples: '0.01 + 3 * 0.025, 0.15' or '10 * 0.025' <cnt> an integer representing the amount of time an offset is repeated <time> a double or integer representing the distance between offsets

outputs.name: Skeleton
outputs.desc: The 2d skeleton of the provided polyline

outputs.name: Offsets
outputs.desc: The offsets

name: Polygon Partition
desc: Divides a simple planar polygon into non-overlapping convex components using Bayazit's convex decomposition algorithm.

inputs.name: Polygon
inputs.desc: A simple non-self-intersecting planar polygon to partition.

outputs.name: Convex Polygons
outputs.desc: A list of non-overlapping convex subdivisions.

name: Polygon Width
desc: Computes the minimum width of a planar polygon from its convex hull and returns the two support lines for the best antipodal configuration.

inputs.name: Polyline
inputs.desc: Closed planar polyline.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Reference plane of the polygon.

outputs.name: Width
outputs.desc: Minimum polygon width.

outputs.name: Support A
outputs.desc: Support line on one side of the minimum-width direction.

outputs.name: Support B
outputs.desc: Support line on the opposite side of the minimum-width direction.

outputs.name: Convex Hull
outputs.desc: Convex hull used in the computation.

name: Random Hamilton Path
desc: Generates a random hamiltonian path from a seed zig-zag horizontal or vertical path by cutting and rotation parallel links

inputs.name: Columns
inputs.desc: Number of columns

inputs.name: Rows
inputs.desc: Number of rows

inputs.name: Steps
inputs.desc: Number of randomization steps

inputs.name: Increment X
inputs.desc: Increment or decrement from the start point in the X direction. True for increment.

inputs.name: Increment Y
inputs.desc: Increment or decrement from the start point in the Y direction. True for increment.

inputs.name: Horizontal
inputs.desc: Create the seed zig-zag path in the horizontal or vertical direction. True for horizontal.

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.desc: Seed for random value.

outputs.name: Path
outputs.desc: The randomized hamiltonian path

name: GraphML To Polyline
desc: Convert a GraphML polyline to a Rhino Polyline

inputs.name: Path
inputs.desc: the path to the graphml file

outputs.name: Polyline
outputs.desc: The polyline

outputs.name: Weigths
outputs.desc: weights

name: Roofer
desc: Build a roof from a closed planar polygon

inputs.name: Polyline
inputs.desc: A planar polyline

inputs.name: Slopes
inputs.desc: A list of slope values. Slope is the cotangent of the angle. Note that 0 slope is a vertical wall

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: The plane where the curve lies

inputs.name: Type
inputs.desc: True for Multiplicative weights (edge speed = w) and false for Additive weights (edge speed = 1 + wa)

outputs.name: Roof
outputs.desc: A mesh with the roof shape

name: Shift PolyCurve Seam
desc: Snaps the seam of a closed polycurve to a kink and shifts it by a number of kinks.

inputs.name: PolyCurve
inputs.desc: Closed polycurve whose seam will be shifted.

inputs.name: Steps
inputs.desc: Kinks to move in curve direction. Zero snaps to the nearest kink.

outputs.name: PolyCurve
outputs.desc: Polycurve with its seam at the selected kink.

outputs.name: Seam
outputs.desc: New seam point.

name: Skeleton2d
desc: Get the 2d skeleton of a planar polygon

inputs.name: Polyline
inputs.desc: A planar polyline

inputs.name: Weights
inputs.desc: list of weights per edge, by default a constant weight of 1 is assumed for all sides. Weights can be understood as the cotangent of the roof angle.

inputs.name: Type
inputs.desc: True for Multiplicative weights (edge speed = w) and false for Additive weights (edge speed = 1 + wa)

inputs.name: Direction
inputs.desc: Skeleton side selection: inside = 0, outside = 1, both = 2

outputs.name: Skeleton
outputs.desc: The 2d skeleton of the provided polyline

outputs.name: Ipe output
outputs.desc: The command result in ipe format

name: Symmetric Subdivision
desc: Subdivides a length by maximizing the use of a preferred maximum module length while distributing the remainder symmetrically to both ends.

inputs.name: Length
inputs.desc: Total length to subdivide.

inputs.name: Max Length
inputs.desc: Preferred maximum module length.

inputs.name: Min Length
inputs.desc: Minimum acceptable end-segment length.

outputs.name: Centers
outputs.desc: Segment center positions measured from zero.

outputs.name: Lengths
outputs.desc: Segment lengths.

outputs.name: Count
outputs.desc: Number of segments.

name: T Component
desc: Creates the closed polyline of a T corner connection from a construction plane, three arm directions, per-arm widths and per-arm minimum member lengths measured beyond the joint geometry.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Construction plane. Its origin defines the component center.

inputs.name: Vector A
inputs.desc: First arm direction.

inputs.name: Vector B
inputs.desc: Second arm direction.

inputs.name: Vector C
inputs.desc: Third arm direction.

inputs.name: Widths
inputs.desc: Per-arm widths. If fewer values are provided than arms, the last value is repeated.

inputs.name: Min Member Lengths
inputs.desc: Per-arm minimum member lengths measured beyond the resolved joint. If fewer values are provided than arms, the last value is repeated.

outputs.name: Polyline
outputs.desc: Closed T-component polyline.

outputs.name: Vertices
outputs.desc: Polyline vertices in order.

name: Three-Segment Arch
desc: Constructs a three-segment arch from a span, a rise, and a construction plane.

inputs.name: Span
inputs.desc: Overall width of the arch.

inputs.name: Rise
inputs.desc: Vertical height from the spring line to the apex.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.desc: Construction plane. Span follows the X axis and rise follows the Y axis.

outputs.name: Arch
outputs.desc: Three-segment polycurve arch.

outputs.name: Arc Segments
outputs.desc: The three individual arc segments from left to right.

outputs.name: Centers
outputs.desc: Centers of the three arc segments.

outputs.name: Joints
outputs.desc: Spring points and junction points between consecutive arc segments.

outputs.name: Apex
outputs.desc: Apex point of the arch.

name: Write GraphML
desc: Write GraphML files

inputs.name: Polyline
inputs.desc: A polyline

inputs.name: Weights
inputs.desc: A list of weights per edge, by default a constant weight of 1 is assumed for all sides. Weights can be understood as the cotangent of the roof angle.

inputs.name: Type
inputs.desc: True for Multiplicative weights (edge speed = w) and false for Additive weights (edge speed = 1 + wa)

inputs.name: Dir
inputs.desc: path to save the file

inputs.name: Filename
inputs.desc: the filename

inputs.name: Save
inputs.desc: Save the file

outputs.name: Xml
outputs.desc: a string with the graphml
